title: Interpreting Spatial Methods Workbench outputs
kicker: DETAILED LOCAL TRAINING · v0.2.1
body:
Design → estimand → uncertainty → biological hypothesis → evidence boundary

A publication-grounded interpretation framework for all 12 workflows
narration: This detailed local training course explains how to discuss Spatial Methods Workbench outputs with scientific collaborators. It is not an automated interpretation service, clinical guidance, or a substitute for the full publications. For every workflow, we will identify the statistical estimand, the quantities reported by the Workbench or source method, the uncertainty or validation needed, the kind of biological hypothesis the result may motivate, and the claims the result cannot establish. Always begin with the observational unit, sampling hierarchy, preprocessing, coordinate system, and scientific question.

title: Use five layers in every explanation
kicker: INTERPRETATION DISCIPLINE
body:
1  Design and preprocessing
2  Statistical estimand
3  Uncertainty, validation, or stability
4  Biologically plausible hypothesis
5  Alternatives and required follow-up
narration: Use five layers in this order. First, state what one observation represents, how observations are nested, and how raw measurements became the analysis table. Second, name the estimand in plain language. Third, describe uncertainty, permutation, posterior selection, bootstrap, held-out error, or stability. Fourth, state a biological hypothesis using cautious language such as consistent with or may motivate. Fifth, name technical and biological alternatives and the replication, perturbation, orthogonal assay, or prospective design needed for a stronger claim.

title: First reconstruct the data-generating process
kicker: BEFORE READING ANY NUMBER
body:
Unit: cell, spot, voxel, contour, subject, slide, or volume?
Hierarchy: what is nested within patient, specimen, site, or time?
Processing: segmentation, registration, normalization, masks, exclusions?
Geometry: coordinate units, boundaries, anisotropy, section spacing?
narration: Interpretation fails when the analyst starts from the result table rather than the data-generating process. Identify the unit represented by a row and the independent biological replicate. Describe nesting within patients, specimens, slides, sites, times, or volumes. Reconstruct segmentation, registration, normalization, transformations, masks, and exclusions. For spatial and volumetric data, record coordinate units, tissue boundaries, anisotropy, section spacing, and missing regions. A statistically correct calculation can still answer the wrong scientific question if the sampling hierarchy or geometry is misunderstood.

title: Moran's I: what quantity is being estimated?
kicker: WORKFLOW 1 · I, WEIGHTS, AND EXPECTATION
body:
I compares weighted cross-products of centered values with total variation
W defines which locations are neighbors and how strongly
Expected I under randomization depends on sample size
Global I summarizes the whole domain—not a local hotspot map
narration: Moran's I is a global spatial autocorrelation statistic. It compares weighted cross-products of centered observations with overall squared variation, scaled by the spatial weight matrix. The graph is therefore part of the estimand: an eight-neighbor result is not the same quantity as a distance-band result. Positive I indicates neighboring similarity under that graph, negative I indicates neighboring dissimilarity, and values near the randomization expectation indicate little global structure. It summarizes the full domain and does not locate the specific region creating the pattern.

title: Moran's I: uncertainty and biological framing
kicker: PERMUTATION p IS CONDITIONAL ON EXCHANGEABILITY
body:
Report: I, graph construction, n, permutations, seed, p-value
Check: alternate k or distance bands, boundaries, density, technical gradients
Respect: patient, slide, specimen, region, or time blocks
Say: spatially structured under the specified graph
narration: The permutation p-value measures how extreme the observed statistic is under the chosen label-exchange scheme. Its credibility depends on exchangeability. If rows share a patient, slide, specimen, batch, region, or time point, unrestricted permutation can create a false reference distribution. Report the statistic, graph, sample count, number of permutations, seed, and p-value. Repeat plausible graphs and examine boundaries and sampling density. A biologically disciplined statement is that the feature is spatially structured under the specified graph. Do not infer a cellular mechanism from global autocorrelation alone.

title: Partial-correlation networks: matrix quantities
kicker: WORKFLOW 2 · COVARIANCE, PRECISION, PARTIAL r
body:
Covariance Σ describes marginal co-variation
Precision Ω = Σ⁻¹ describes conditional structure
Partial rᵢⱼ = −Ωᵢⱼ / √(ΩᵢᵢΩⱼⱼ)
Ridge penalty stabilizes inversion
Threshold converts a continuous matrix into a displayed graph
narration: The conditional-network screen estimates a covariance matrix, applies a ridge penalty, inverts it to obtain a precision matrix, and standardizes the off-diagonal precision entries as partial correlations. A partial correlation is the residual linear association between two included variables after conditioning on the other included variables. The ridge penalty is not merely numerical housekeeping; it changes the estimate, especially with correlated features or limited observations. The graph threshold is a decision applied to a continuous matrix. Preserve and inspect the matrix rather than interpreting only the displayed edges.

title: Partial networks: from an edge to a hypothesis
kicker: CONDITIONAL ASSOCIATION IS NOT MECHANISM
body:
Positive edge → conditional coordination
Negative edge → conditional opposition
No displayed edge → below threshold, not proven absence
Possible hypotheses: shared niche, exclusion, coordinated state
Alternatives: composition, omitted variables, batch, transformation, instability
narration: A positive edge describes conditional coordination and a negative edge conditional opposition under the fitted linear model. An absent displayed edge means the estimate fell below the chosen rule, not that biology is absent. An edge may motivate hypotheses about a shared niche, exclusion, or coordinated state. It does not establish physical contact, signaling, regulation, direction, or causation. Review transformations, outliers, feature panel composition, ridge sensitivity, sample size, zone sizes, thresholds, and omitted variables. Report the continuous estimate with the exact model and threshold used.

title: ISPat 2D: quantities in the publication
kicker: WORKFLOW 3 · SPATIAL INTENSITIES AND MULTI-STUDY FACTORS
body:
Marker or cell-type spatial intensity surfaces
Shared covariance/loading structure across regions
Region-specific covariance/loading deviations
Partial correlations and positive/negative edge signs
Across-sample proportions carrying each edge sign
narration: The ISPat publication first characterizes spatial intensity surfaces and then uses multi-study factor structure to separate shared from region-specific covariance patterns. Publication-level summaries include shared and zone-specific covariance or loading quantities, partial-correlation matrices, thresholded positive and negative edges, and proportions of samples in which an edge sign occurs. In simulations, recovery is also summarized with an RV coefficient comparing matrices. These quantities address spatially adjusted conditional organization; they are richer than a separate network fit within each zone.

title: ISPat 2D: explain shared versus zone-specific
kicker: THE DECOMPOSITION DEFINES THE SCIENTIFIC LANGUAGE
body:
Shared pattern → modeled organization conserved across zones
Zone-specific pattern → deviation associated with a prespecified domain
Edge proportion → reproducibility across modeled samples
Thresholded sign → a summary of a continuous estimate
narration: Explain a shared pattern as conditional organization conserved across the modeled zones, and a zone-specific pattern as a deviation associated with a prespecified domain. An across-sample edge proportion summarizes how often a sign is recovered under the paper's aggregation rule; it is not the posterior probability of a universal biological law. Thresholded edge signs summarize continuous estimates. In the pancreatic application, tumor-intensity zones and epithelial, APC, CTL, T-helper, and Treg features provided the biological context. For a new assay, those labels and zones must be independently justified.

title: ISPat 2D: checks before biological discussion
kicker: SPATIAL ADJUSTMENT DOES NOT REMOVE EVERY CONFOUNDER
body:
Verify phenotype definitions and measurement scales
Justify zones independently of the desired network result
Inspect intensity surfaces, matrices, edge signs, and thresholds
Review priors, chains, convergence, and observations per zone
Seek replication and functional validation
narration: Before interpreting ISPat biology, verify phenotype or marker definitions, normalization, and spatial units. Ensure zones were defined independently of the desired result and have adequate observations across biological replicates. Inspect the fitted intensity surfaces, continuous matrices, thresholded signs, and sample-level heterogeneity. Review prior choices, chain behavior, effective sample size, convergence, and sensitivity to thresholds and bandwidths. The ISPat authors describe the networks as conditional dependencies. Functional validation, orthogonal assays, and replication remain necessary for mechanistic claims.

title: GP-GHS: what the model selects
kicker: WORKFLOW 4 · SPATIAL EDGE FIELDS AND GROUPED SHRINKAGE
body:
Each candidate edge is represented over space with basis coefficients
Grouped horseshoe shrinkage acts on the edge as a group
Adjacency summarizes a posterior selection rule
The fitted object retains location-specific edge behavior
narration: GP-GHS represents a candidate conditional-dependence edge as a spatially varying field through basis coefficients. Grouped horseshoe shrinkage acts jointly on the coefficients for an edge, allowing the method to suppress unsupported edge functions while retaining spatially structured ones. A Workbench adjacency is a compact summary of the configured posterior selection rule. It does not fully describe the edge's sign, magnitude, uncertainty, or spatial variation. Those properties live in the detailed fitted object and must be inspected at locations or regions relevant to the scientific question.

title: GP-GHS: uncertainty, sensitivity, and wording
kicker: SELECTED EDGE ≠ UNIFORM EDGE
body:
Review basis dimension, smoothness, coordinate scaling, chains, ESS, R-hat
Check threshold and symmetry rules
Map posterior edge fields with tissue boundaries and uncertainty
Say: evidence for a spatially structured conditional relationship
narration: A selected GP-GHS edge does not imply the same sign or magnitude everywhere. Review basis dimension, smoothness, coordinate scaling, tissue boundaries, chain mixing, effective sample sizes, convergence statistics, selection threshold, and symmetry rule. Map the detailed posterior edge field with uncertainty and compare results across reasonable settings and biological specimens. Appropriate language is that the model found evidence for a spatially structured conditional relationship. Regional biological labels should be applied only after independent annotation and should not turn a conditional association into a direction or mechanism.

title: ISPat 3D: volumetric quantities
kicker: WORKFLOW 5 · 3D TREND, SHARED MATRIX, ZONE MATRIX
body:
Marker-specific 3D spatial adjustment
Multi-study factor decomposition
Shared and zone-specific covariance or partial-correlation structure
Per-volume fitted objects and edge summaries
narration: ISPat 3D extends marker-specific spatial adjustment and multi-study network estimation to registered volumes or serial sections. Its scientific quantities include three-dimensional spatial trends and shared or zone-specific covariance and partial-correlation structure, retained within per-volume fitted objects. A shared volumetric edge describes conditional organization conserved across the modeled domains, while a zone-specific edge describes a modeled deviation in a domain. The z axis and volume identifiers are scientific variables, not merely columns needed to pass readiness.

title: ISPat 3D: registration is part of inference
kicker: A 3D NETWORK IS ONLY AS CREDIBLE AS ITS GEOMETRY
body:
Check orientation, section order, thickness, spacing, and anisotropy
Review registration error, missing sections, masks, and tissue deformation
Assess staining drift and volume-to-volume heterogeneity
Distinguish depth biology from reconstruction artifacts
narration: Three-dimensional interpretation begins with geometry. Verify orientation, section order, thickness, spacing, anisotropy, registration error, missing sections, masks, deformations, and coordinate units. Examine staining drift and heterogeneity across volumes. A depth-dependent edge can arise from real volumetric organization, but also from misregistration, discontinuous sampling, or technical drift. Review the spatial adjustment and full matrices within each volume, and replicate across independent volumes. State a volumetric conditional pattern before proposing a biological mechanism.

title: Linear and logistic prediction: performance quantities
kicker: WORKFLOW 6 · ERROR, PROBABILITY, CALIBRATION
body:
Continuous: RMSE, MAE, held-out R², residuals
Binary: predicted probability, accuracy, sensitivity/specificity as added analyses
Coefficients: conditional predictive associations under the model
Performance is conditional on the validation split
narration: For continuous outcomes, RMSE emphasizes large errors, MAE reports average absolute error, and held-out R squared compares predictive variation under the test design. For binary outcomes, predicted probabilities are primary; accuracy depends on the cutoff and prevalence and should be supplemented with discrimination and calibration where appropriate. Coefficients are conditional predictive associations under the fitted model, not causal effects. Every metric is conditional on the test population and split. Report its denominator, uncertainty, prevalence, and any preprocessing learned exclusively from training data.

title: Prediction: structured validation comes first
kicker: RANDOM ROW SPLITS CAN LEAK BIOLOGY AND SPACE
body:
Block by patient, specimen, slide, site, time, or spatial region
Keep preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning inside training folds
Compare simple baselines and assess calibration
Prefer external replication for generalization claims
narration: Spatial and biomedical records are structured. If neighboring locations or observations from one patient or slide occur in both training and test sets, the model can appear to generalize while memorizing shared context. Use patient, specimen, slide, site, time, or spatial blocks appropriate to deployment. Perform normalization, feature selection, and tuning inside the training folds. Compare with transparent baselines, quantify calibration and subgroup performance, and seek an external cohort. Predictive accuracy does not explain why the outcome occurs.

title: Spatial clustering: understand the constructed geometry
kicker: WORKFLOW 7 · FEATURES + WEIGHTED COORDINATES
body:
Standardized biological features define one distance component
Scaled coordinates define another
Spatial weight controls their trade-off
Assignments, centers, and between/total ratio summarize k-means
narration: The spatial clustering path performs k-means in a constructed space containing standardized biological features and coordinates multiplied by the selected spatial weight. The weight changes the question: zero emphasizes feature similarity, while larger values favor geographic compactness. Assignments and centers describe the algorithmic partition, and the between-to-total sum-of-squares ratio is an internal separation measure. It does not validate the cluster count or biological identity. Study stability across seeds, feature sets, transformations, cluster counts, and spatial weights before assigning any biological label.

title: Shallow neural prediction: what can be claimed
kicker: WORKFLOW 8 · NONLINEAR SCREENING
body:
Outputs: held-out predictions, errors or probabilities, fitted network
Controls: hidden units, weight decay, seed, split
Weights are distributed parameters—not direct effects
Compare with linear/logistic baselines under the same blocked validation
narration: The shallow neural workflow asks whether a compact nonlinear predictor improves held-out performance. Hidden units control representation capacity, weight decay regularizes parameters, and the seed influences initialization and splitting. Individual network weights are distributed across layers and should not be narrated as direct biological effects. Compare the model with linear or logistic baselines under identical grouped validation, repeat seeds, assess calibration, and use separate attribution methods only with their own stability checks. A performance gain supports nonlinear predictive structure, not a learned mechanism.

title: Scalar-image screen: Workbench quantities
kicker: WORKFLOW 9 · RIDGE COEFFICIENTS AND HELD-OUT ERROR
body:
Standardized ridge coefficients rank conditional predictive contributions
RMSE and MAE evaluate scalar prediction
Penalty distributes weight across correlated aligned features
Coefficient maps depend on scaling, mask, alignment, and penalty
narration: The Workbench scalar-image path is a ridge screen. It relates aligned high-dimensional image or voxel features to a scalar outcome, reports standardized penalized coefficients, and evaluates held-out RMSE and MAE. A coefficient is a contribution to the penalized linear predictor conditional on the other included features and chosen scaling. Correlated pixels can divide or redistribute signal, and magnitude ranking is not a posterior probability. Inspect coefficient stability, residuals, masks, alignment, site effects, and penalty selection.

title: Scalar-image publications: do not conflate quantities
kicker: SV-NN AND ST-CAR ARE FULL SPATIAL MODELS
body:
Publication quantities may include spatial effect surfaces
Active regions or voxels
Posterior inclusion or selection measures
Spatial uncertainty and structured priors

A Workbench ridge rank is not posterior-selected evidence
narration: The related SV-NN and ST-CAR publications estimate spatially structured effect surfaces, active regions, posterior selection or inclusion quantities, and uncertainty under explicit spatial models. Those are not the same as the Workbench ridge coefficients. Do not describe a ranked ridge feature as posterior-selected, spatially smoothed, or causal. Use the screen to identify predictive structure and motivate a fuller analysis. When the scientific target is spatial selection with posterior uncertainty, fit the appropriate publication-level model and report its priors, posterior summaries, diagnostics, and sensitivity.

title: Image-to-image screen: latent quantities
kicker: WORKFLOW 10 · SCORES, LOADINGS, RECONSTRUCTION
body:
Separate PCA bases summarize source and target variation
Regression links subject-level latent scores
Loadings map factors back to aligned features
Held-out RMSE measures reconstructed target error
narration: The Workbench image-to-image screen constructs separate PCA bases for aligned source and target images, regresses target scores on source scores, reconstructs target features, and reports held-out reconstruction error. Scores position subjects along variance directions and loadings map those directions to features. A factor is a mathematical direction of variation, not automatically a pathway or anatomical process. Interpret factors only after visualizing loadings and reconstructions, checking sign conventions and stability, and relating patterns to independently established anatomy or biology.

title: Image-to-image publications: SBLF distinction
kicker: SCREENING PCA IS NOT A SPATIAL BAYESIAN LATENT FACTOR MODEL
body:
SBLF uses spatial Bayesian latent factors
It estimates spatially varying regression structure and posterior uncertainty
Workbench uses separate PCA plus score regression
Use identical masks, resolution, registration, and leakage-free factor tuning
narration: The SBLF publication uses spatial Bayesian latent factors and spatially varying regression coefficients with posterior uncertainty. The Workbench screen uses separate principal component bases and score regression. These are different inferential objects. Use the Workbench result as a fast reconstruction and prediction screen, not as an SBLF posterior. Confirm identical masks, resolution, orientation, registration, feature order, and subject alignment. Choose factor counts without test leakage, inspect residual images and per-feature error, and use the full SBLF method when spatial posterior inference is required.

title: Mediation: define the three reported effects
kicker: WORKFLOW 11 · INDIRECT, DIRECT, TOTAL
body:
Indirect = a × b in the fitted linear models
Direct = exposure coefficient with mediator included
Total = exposure coefficient without mediator
Bootstrap interval describes resampling variability
narration: The mediation screen fits an exposure-to-mediator model and outcome models with and without the mediator. The indirect effect is the product a times b in the fitted linear specification. The direct effect is the exposure coefficient with the mediator included, and the total effect is the exposure coefficient without it. A percentile bootstrap interval summarizes resampling variability under the observed design. It does not prove that the pathway is causally identified or that the mediator transmits a physical mechanism.

title: Mediation: identification before causal language
kicker: SEQUENTIAL IGNORABILITY IS NOT TESTED BY THE APP
body:
Require temporal ordering, consistency, positivity, and defensible confounding control
Address clustering, exposure–mediator interaction, and model form
Perform sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding
Say: model-based indirect association unless identification is justified
narration: Causal mediation requires more than a nonzero product. Exposure must precede mediator and mediator precede outcome; consistency and positivity must be plausible; exposure-outcome, exposure-mediator, and mediator-outcome confounding must be addressed; and model form, clustering, and exposure-mediator interaction may matter. Use sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding. Without these conditions, say the data are consistent with a model-based indirect association. Reserve causal mediation language for a design and analysis that explicitly support identification.

title: Shape PCA: quantities after geometric preprocessing
kicker: WORKFLOW 12 · SCORES, LOADINGS, EXPLAINED VARIANCE
body:
Contours are resampled, centered, and size-normalized
PC scores place contours along modes
Loadings describe coordinated landmark movement
Explained variance describes sample geometry—not biological importance
narration: The shape path resamples ordered contours, removes translation and scale, and applies PCA to the landmark-coordinate vectors. A component score positions a contour along a geometric mode. A loading describes coordinated landmark movement, and explained variance measures geometric variability within the processed sample. It does not measure aggressiveness, prognosis, or biological importance. Interpret each mode by plotting mean shape plus and minus component multiples, and report the preprocessing choices that define the shape space.

title: Shape PCA: correspondence and rotation checks
kicker: GEOMETRIC ARTIFACTS CAN DOMINATE COMPONENTS
body:
Verify contour direction and starting-point correspondence
Assess segmentation repeatability and missing boundaries
State whether rotation was standardized
Separate acquisition orientation from intrinsic morphology
Validate any outcome association in a new model and cohort
narration: Shape components can be dominated by technical correspondence. Verify clockwise or counterclockwise contour direction, starting-point alignment, landmark correspondence, segmentation repeatability, and treatment of incomplete boundaries. State whether rotation was standardized; the Workbench does not automatically remove every rotational difference. Decide whether orientation is a biological feature or an acquisition artifact. Any link between a shape score and disease or outcome belongs in a separate model with grouped validation and independent replication.

title: A collaborator-ready reporting template
kicker: USE THE SAME LOGIC FOR EVERY WORKFLOW
body:
We analyzed [unit] using [workflow] to estimate [quantity].
Under [settings/design], the estimate was [value + uncertainty].
This supports [statistical statement].
It is consistent with—but does not establish—[hypothesis].
A stronger claim requires [specific validation].
narration: Use this structure in meetings, reports, and manuscripts. We analyzed the stated observational unit using the named workflow to estimate a specific quantity. Under the recorded settings and validation design, the estimate was the reported value with uncertainty. This supports a precise statistical statement. It is consistent with, but does not establish, a named biological hypothesis. Then list the main alternative explanations and the exact independent cohort, blocked validation, perturbation, orthogonal assay, functional experiment, or prospective design required for a stronger claim.

title: Red-flag phrases and disciplined replacements
kicker: LANGUAGE IS PART OF STATISTICAL QUALITY CONTROL
body:
Avoid: proves interaction → Prefer: conditional association
Avoid: causal voxel → Prefer: screening coefficient or posterior-selected region
Avoid: true cell state → Prefer: algorithmic cluster
Avoid: learned mechanism → Prefer: held-out predictive structure
Avoid: mediated pathway → Prefer: model-based indirect effect
narration: Language can overstate evidence even when the computation is correct. Replace proves interaction with conditional association. Replace causal voxel with screening coefficient, or with posterior-selected region only when a full posterior method supports that term. Replace true cell state with algorithmic cluster until externally validated. Replace learned mechanism with held-out predictive structure. Replace mediated pathway with model-based indirect effect unless causal assumptions are defended. These substitutions retain scientific value while making the evidence boundary explicit.

title: Final interpretation checklist
kicker: PRESERVE THE CHAIN FROM DATA TO CLAIM
body:
Design and preprocessing documented
Estimand and method quantity named correctly
Uncertainty, diagnostics, and sensitivity reviewed
Biological hypothesis separated from mechanism
Alternative explanations and follow-up stated
Bundle, fitted object, code version, and citations archived
narration: Before presenting a result, verify that design and preprocessing are documented, the estimand and method-specific quantity are named correctly, and uncertainty, diagnostics, sensitivity, and sampling hierarchy have been reviewed. Separate a biologically plausible hypothesis from mechanism or causation. State competing explanations and the follow-up needed to distinguish them. Archive the result bundle, fitted object, code and package versions, data checksum, and method citations. For study-specific interpretation, return to the full local guide and source publication and involve experts who understand the assay, tissue, disease, and design.
